prose:
On Cheeky Pint, Sam Altman tells John Collison why he is against a single superintelligence, across a wide-ranging conversation with a published transcript. The technical highlights: Altman discusses how OpenAI's models uncovered critical vulnerabilities in PHP - a twenty-year-old codebase - during what he calls 'PHP week', why test-time compute unlocks massive agent swarms, and internal experiments he says prove the models on complex math problems like Navier-Stokes. He calls sandboxing superhuman models an unsolved safety dilemma.

The rest is industry economics: robotics scaling future gigawatt data centers, revenue per gigawatt as the metric that matters, the claim that 'token pricing is fake', and a prediction that personal agents will replace traditional web forms and mobile apps, forcing businesses to adapt.

'PHP week': OpenAI models uncovered critical vulnerabilities in 20-year-old PHP code
Test-time compute unlocks massive agent swarms; internal math results include Navier-Stokes

Robotics will scale gigawatt data centers; revenue per gigawatt is the metric
"Token pricing is fake"; personal agents to replace web forms and mobile apps
